# Temple Scroll Column 57 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 57 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**57:1** When he sits on the throne of his kingdom, they shall write for him this Torah on a scroll, from the one that is before the priests.

**57:2** This is the Torah they shall write for him: he shall not [...] and he shall not add to what I command him, nor diminish from it.

**57:3** He shall read in it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear Me and to keep all these words and to observe them.

**57:4** His heart shall not be exalted above his brothers, nor shall he turn aside from what I command, to the right or to the left,

**57:5** so that he may prolong his days in his kingdom, he and his sons after him, in the midst of Israel.

**57:6** He shall select from among all his brothers one thousand per tribe to serve with him — twelve thousand warriors —

**57:7** who shall not leave him alone, lest he be captured by the nations.

**57:8** All the men he selects shall be men of integrity, God-fearing, who despise dishonest gain — men of valor.

**57:9** They shall be with him continually, day and night, guarding him from every sinful deed

**57:10** and from every foreign influence, so that he does not fall into their power.

**57:11** He shall have a council of twelve princes of his people, together with twelve priests and twelve Levites,

**57:12** who shall sit with him for matters of judgment and Torah.

**57:13** His heart shall not be exalted above theirs, and he shall not undertake anything without their counsel, in any matter whatsoever.

**57:14** He shall not take a wife from among the daughters of the nations, but from his father's house he shall take a wife, from his father's family.

**57:15** He shall not take another wife in addition to her, for she alone shall be with him all the days of her life.

**57:16** If she dies, he may take another wife from his father's house, from his family.

**57:17** He shall not pervert justice; he shall accept no bribe; he shall not covet a field or a vineyard, any property or house, or any desirable thing in Israel.

**57:18** He shall not seize [...] any possession of the people.

**57:19** He shall not amass silver and gold beyond what is necessary, but only what is sufficient.

**57:20** When the trumpet of alarm sounds for war, he shall march out at their head, and when the trumpet of assembly sounds, they shall gather to him.

**57:21** He shall take counsel with them and not act alone without their counsel in any matter of war.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 57 contains the Temple Scroll's unique expansion of the Law of the King. The royal guard of 12,000 warriors (57:6-7), the council of 36 (57:11-12), and the strict monogamy requirement (57:15-16) have no Deuteronomic parallels. This legislation likely reflects sectarian critique of Hasmonean royal practices. The king is subordinated to Torah and council at every turn.*
